title: Approximate Nearest-Neighbor Indexes: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Approximate Nearest-Neighbor Indexes: Visual Guide

1. One Dot Product, N Times | the bridge from the dual-tower comparison to the search problem: a corpus-size slider showing coordinate multiplications and float32 bytes, plus a toggle between one live query and a 2,000-query exact ground-truth sweep | exact k-NN costs work proportional to N times d, so 10M 768-dim vectors is 7.68 billion multiplications and 30.72 GB, and no fixed corpus size automatically requires approximation - exact search survives as the frozen baseline that ANN recall@k is measured against

2. The nprobe Dial | an IVF space of cells with a list-count segment (100 to 100,000) and an nprobe slider, showing per-list size, candidates scanned, centroid comparisons and percent of corpus, plus a boundary-query toggle that misses at nprobe 1 | k-means centroids route the query so 1,000,000 vectors over 1,000 cells means probing 10 touches about 1% of the corpus, and nprobe exists to repair the boundary miss where the true neighbor was assigned to the cell next door

3. Walking The Layers | a three-layer HNSW graph stepped hop by hop from entry node A through F and M down to the bottom layer, with an efSearch segment (20 / 80 / 200) that changes where the same walk ends | greedy traversal uses upper-layer edges as shortcuts and can still stop at a local best, because geometric adjacency is not graph adjacency - only a wider candidate frontier carries the worse-scoring node that leads to the true nearest

4. Ninety-Six Bytes | a product-quantization builder with a subspace slider and a codebook-size segment, showing code bytes against the raw 3,072, compression ratio, lookup-table entries and per-candidate lookups and adds | splitting 768 dims into 96 groups of 8 with 256 centroids each gives one byte per group - 96 bytes for 32x compression - and asymmetric distance computation builds a 24,576-entry table once per query so scoring becomes 96 lookups and 95 adds instead of 768 multiplications

5. Pick An Operating Point | the efSearch sweep (0.91 at 8 ms, 0.975 at 21 ms, 0.992 at 48 ms) selected by a latency-budget slider, with storage and replica toggles driving a memory bar | there is no universal best setting: the operating point falls out of the stage's service objective, memory is far more than the vectors, and ANN recall is agreement with exact search rather than evidence that useful documents reached the candidate set
